content.text:
In OAuth2, a **refresh** is the background HTTP request the client library makes to Google to trade the long-lived **refresh token** for a brand new short-lived **access token**, without involving the browser or the user again.

Concretely, in this codebase:

- `drive_token.json` on disk stores two things: an `access_token` (used on every Drive API call, expires after ~1 hour) and a `refresh_token` (long-lived, used to mint new access tokens).
- When you call `src.Token()`, the oauth2 library checks if the access token you loaded from disk is still valid. If it's expired, it silently calls Google's token endpoint with the refresh token and gets back a **new access token** (this HTTP round-trip is "the refresh"). The refresh token itself is normally reused as-is.
- `fresh` is whatever `src.Token()` returns — either the *same* token you loaded (if it was still valid) or a *new* one (if a refresh just happened). The code can't tell which case it is from the outside, hence "may have."

The comment is explaining why we bother writing `fresh` back to `drive_token.json`: if a refresh did happen, the access token on disk is now stale, so we persist the new one — otherwise the next call would needlessly refresh again over the network.

Each call goes through `driveClient` → `driveRunOAuthFlow`, and `driveRunOAuthFlow` unconditionally binds the hardcoded port 8765 with no locking. The first goroutine wins the bind and completes the flow (or refresh) successfully; the second's bind fails with exactly `listen tcp :8765: bind: address already in use`, and that error lands on the root node — hence a *successful* fetch alongside a stray error under the root.

This isn't StrictMode-only, either: any two Drive calls racing while a token needs (re-)authentication would hit the same problem. The right fix is to serialize `driveClient` so only one goroutine ever runs the refresh/OAuth-flow logic at a time; a second caller should just wait and reuse the result instead of racing to bind its own listener.

**Root cause:** `DriveFolderPickerModal`'s root tree node auto-loads via a bare `useEffect(() => { load() }, [])` (`DriveFolderPickerModal.tsx:41-44`). React's `StrictMode` (on in `main.tsx`) double-invokes mount effects in dev, so two `ListDriveFolder('root')` calls fire almost simultaneously. Each goes through `driveClient`, and whenever a refresh/full OAuth flow is needed, `driveRunOAuthFlow` unconditionally binds port 8765 for the callback server — first caller wins the bind and succeeds, the second gets `bind: address already in use`, and that error surfaces under the root node even though the sibling call succeeded.

**Fix:** serialized `driveClient` with a package-level `driveClientMu sync.Mutex` (`drive_auth.go`), so only one goroutine ever runs the refresh/OAuth-flow logic at a time. A blocked second caller re-enters after the first finishes, finds the now-valid persisted token on disk, and succeeds without racing for the port. This also covers the general case (not just StrictMode) — any two concurrent Drive calls needing re-auth would have hit this before.
